newsitem.title: MEXICO: Telmex leads balloting in Puebla, Hermosillo.
newsitem.headline: Telmex leads balloting in Puebla, Hermosillo.

text.p: Former Mexican telephone monopoly Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) was firmly ahead in pre-subscription balloting for long-distance carriers in the cities of Puebla and Hermosillo, officials said on Wednesday.
In the central city of Puebla, Telmex had won 49,190, or 65.02 percent, of 75,656 ballots returned as of March 3, the Federal Telecommunications Commission (Cofetel) said in a statement.
Alestra, a joint venture between AT&T and Mexico's Grupo Financiero Banamex-Accival, won 16,049 of the ballots, or 21.21 percent.
Avantel, a venture between MCI Corp., Mexico's Alfa and holding company VISA-Bancomer, obtained 9,977 of the votes, some 13.19 percent of the total.
The balloting process so far represented some 39.48 percent of Puebla's 191,632 installed lines, Cofetel said.
In the northern city of Hermosillo, Telmex had won 50.23 percent, or 15,722, of the votes, while Alestra garnered 9,739 ballots, or 31.12 percent. Avantel had won 5,717 ballots, or 18.27 percent.
Some 39.87 percent of Hermosillo's 78,496 installed lines had been accounted for, the statement said.
